posts.title: How I plan a month of content in one afternoon
posts.excerpt: My simple system for turning one brainstorm session into 30 days of posts — without burning out.
posts.body:
## Start with one theme

Every month gets one theme. Everything I post ladders back to it — this keeps the feed focused and me sane.

## Batch everything

- Write all captions in one sitting
- Design all graphics in one session
- Film all reels in one shoot day
- Schedule in one calendar block

## Leave room to trend-jack

I plan 80% and leave 20% open for whatever the algorithm is loving that week.

> Consistency beats perfection. Planning beats motivation.

posts.title: My CapCut workflow: raw footage to finished reel in 2 hours
posts.excerpt: The exact steps, presets and shortcuts I use to edit reels fast without them looking fast.
posts.body:
## Organise before you edit

Rename clips by scene, drop markers on the good takes, and delete everything unusable first. Editing starts with a clean bin.

## Cut to the beat

Pick the audio before the visuals. CapCut's beat markers do the heavy lifting — cut on the drop, hold on the hook.

## Polish in one pass

One pass for pacing, one for captions and zooms, one for color. Three passes max, then export. A reel that's 95% done beats one that never ships.

posts.title: Designing graphics that stop the scroll
posts.excerpt: What I've learned about contrast, hierarchy and hook-first layouts from designing hundreds of social graphics.
posts.body:
## The first second decides

You have about one second in the feed. If the message isn't readable without zooming, the design has failed — no matter how pretty it is.

## Contrast is the cheat code

Bold type, one accent color, plenty of negative space. When in doubt, remove an element.

## One graphic, one idea

Each graphic carries exactly one message. If you need to say two things, make two graphics.

> Pretty is optional. Clear is mandatory.
